verses.zh: （耶和华的仆人大卫的诗，交与伶长。）恶人的罪过在他心里说：我眼中不怕　神！
verses.en: For the music director, an oracle, written by the Lord’s servant David.[NOTE:1] An evil man is rebellious to the core.[NOTE:2] He does not fear God,[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 36. Though evil men plan to harm others, the psalmist is confident that the Lord is the just ruler of the earth who gives and sustains all life. He prays for divine blessing and protection and anticipates God’s judgment of the wicked.

In the Hebrew text the word נאם (“oracle”) appears at the beginning of the next verse (v. 2 in the Hebrew text because the superscription is considered v. 1). The resulting reading, “an oracle of rebellion for the wicked [is] in the midst of my heart” (cf. NIV) apparently means that the psalm, which foresees the downfall of the wicked, is a prophetic oracle about the rebellion of the wicked which emerges from the soul of the psalmist. One could translate, “Here is a poem written as I reflected on the rebellious character of evil men.” Another option, followed in the translation above, is to attach נאם (ne’um, “oracle”) with the superscription. For another example of a Davidic poem being labeled an “oracle,” see 2 Sam 23:1.

Heb “[the] rebellion of an evil man [is] in the midst of my heart.” The translation assumes a reading “in the midst of his heart” (i.e., “to the core”) instead of “in the midst of my heart,” a change which finds support in a few medieval Hebrew mss, the Hebrew text of Origen’s Hexapla, and the Syriac.

verses.zh: 他自夸自媚，以为他的罪孽终不显露，不被恨恶。
verses.en: for he is too proudto recognize and give up his sin.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there is no dread of God before his eyes.” The phrase “dread of God” refers here to a healthy respect for God which recognizes that he will punish evil behavior.

verses.zh: 他口中的言语尽是罪孽诡诈；他与智慧善行已经断绝。
verses.en: The words he speaks are sinful and deceitful;he does not care about doing what is wise and right.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for it causes to be smooth to him in his eyes to find his sin to hate.” The meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear. Perhaps the point is this: His rebellious attitude makes him reject any notion that God will hold him accountable. His attitude also prevents him from recognizing and repudiating his sinful ways.

verses.zh: 他在床上图谋罪孽，定意行不善的道，不憎恶恶事。
verses.en: While he lies in bed he plans ways to sin.He is committed to a sinful lifestyle;[NOTE:1] he does not reject what is evil.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he ceases to exhibit wisdom to do good.” The Hiphil forms are exhibitive, indicating the outward expression of an inner attitude.
Heb “he takes a stand in a way [that is] not good.” The word “way” here refers metaphorically to behavior or life style.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的慈爱上及诸天；你的信实达到穹苍。
verses.en: O Lord, your loyal love reaches to the sky,[NOTE:1] your faithfulness to the clouds.[NOTE:2]
notes: The three imperfect verbal forms in v. 4 highlight the characteristic behavior of the typical evildoer.
Heb “[is] in the heavens.”

verses.zh: 你的公义好像高山；你的判断如同深渊。耶和华啊，人民、牲畜，你都救护。
verses.en: Your justice is like the highest mountains,[NOTE:1] your fairness like the deepest sea;you, Lord, preserve[NOTE:2] mankind and the animal kingdom.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Lord’s loyal love/faithfulness is almost limitless. He is loyal and faithful to his creation and blesses mankind and the animal kingdom with physical life and sustenance (vv. 6-9).
Heb “mountains of God.” The divine name אֵל (ʾel, “God”) is here used in an idiomatic manner to indicate the superlative.
Or “deliver.”

verses.zh: 神啊，你的慈爱何其宝贵！世人投靠在你翅膀的荫下。
verses.en: How precious[NOTE:1] is your loyal love, O God!The human race finds shelter under your wings.[NOTE:2]
notes: God’s justice/fairness is firm and reliable like the highest mountains and as abundant as the water in the deepest sea. The psalmist uses a legal metaphor to describe God’s preservation of his creation. Like a just judge who vindicates the innocent, God protects his creation from destructive forces.
Or “valuable.”

verses.zh: 他们必因你殿里的肥甘得以饱足；你也必叫他们喝你乐河的水。
verses.en: They are filled with food from your house,and you allow them to drink from the river of your delicacies.

verses.zh: 因为，在你那里有生命的源头；在你的光中，我们必得见光。
verses.en: For with you is the fountain of life;in your light we see light.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the sons of man in the shadow of your wings find shelter.” The preservation of physical life is in view, as the next verse makes clear.

verses.zh: 愿你常施慈爱给认识你的人，常以公义待心里正直的人。
verses.en: Extend[NOTE:1] your loyal love to your faithful followers,[NOTE:2] and vindicate[NOTE:3] the morally upright.[NOTE:4]
notes: Water (note “fountain”) and light are here metaphors for life.
Heb “draw out to full length.”
Heb “to those who know you.” The Hebrew verb יָדַע (yadaʿ, “know”) is used here of those who “know” the Lord in the sense that they recognize his royal authority and obey his will (see Jer 22:16).
Heb “and your justice to.” The verb “extend” is understood by ellipsis in the second line (see the previous line).

verses.zh: 不容骄傲人的脚践踏我；不容凶恶人的手赶逐我。
verses.en: Do not let arrogant men overtake me,or let evil men make me homeless.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the pure of heart.” The “heart” is here viewed as the seat of one’s moral character and motives. The “pure of heart” are God’s faithful followers who trust in and love the Lord and, as a result, experience his deliverance (see Pss 7:10; 11:2; 32:11; 64:10; 94:15; 97:11).

verses.zh: 在那里，作孽的人已经仆倒；他们被推倒，不能再起来。
verses.en: I can see the evildoers! They have fallen.[NOTE:1] They have been knocked down and are unable to get up.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “let not a foot of pride come to me, and let not the hand of the evil ones cause me to wander as a fugitive.”

Heb “there the workers of wickedness have fallen.” The adverb שָׁם (sham, “there”) is used here for dramatic effect, as the psalmist envisions the evildoers lying fallen at a spot that is vivid in his imagination (BDB 1027 s.v.).
